inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 34,560,675 basic shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (22 Jul 2026) plus ~0.1M dilutive awards (Q2-26 weighted diluted 34.8M vs basic 34.7M). Held FLAT because SBC plus equity-award withholding is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (FY2025 $482M, H1-26 $151M) are the mechanism funding the flat count and are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement (SEC XBRL CIK 1069202): ShareBasedCompensation $29.1M plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $19.2M, summed because Lennox publishes no combined equity-award figure. H1-2026 run-rate $12.1M + $11.4M = 0.88% of revenue.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases $482.3M (plus $19.2M withholding); H1-2026 $151.3M (plus $11.4M withholding). Actual cash spent, not authorisation.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo chart API); 52-week range 350.22-587.27, price sits near the low
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-29) balance sheet at 30 Jun 2026: commercial paper $412.0M + current maturities of long-term debt $20.1M (finance leases) + long-term debt $1,149.2M = $1,581.3M, less cash $51.5M ($0.6M short-term investments ignored). Operating lease liabilities ($443.4M) are EXCLUDED: under ASC 842 the operating-lease cost is inside operating expenses and EBITDA, so charging the liability as well would be the double count. NOTE: the Metrics CSV total_debt column ($1,162M at FY2025/Q1-26) is the LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations tag plus the current finance-lease portion and OMITS commercial paper ($226M FY2025, $361M Q1-26, $412M Q2-26); the DCF uses the full DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations basis.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases as operating cost (treatment B): the full lease expense is already inside GAAP operating income under ASC 842, so EBITDA is post-lease and operating lease liabilities stay out of net debt. Finance leases (~$70M) are financing in substance and sit inside total_debt. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed because no lease cost has been added back.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: Lennox has no material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest/investment income $5.5M is immaterial against $1.53B of net debt (the company is a net borrower, so the 'net cash counted twice' rule does not apply); nothing is deducted. Interest EXPENSE ($40.9M FY2025, $29.9M H1-26) is excluded from the unlevered flows and handled through the WACC.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. 10-year UST ~4.2% (Oct 2026) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.15 for a housing-exposed HVAC OEM gives cost of equity ~10%; after-tax cost of debt ~4% on $1.58B against a ~$12.5B market cap (11% debt weight) gives WACC ~9.3%, rounded to 9.0% and held identical across all three scenarios so cyclical and execution risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows, not again in the rate.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2026-FY2035), chosen because Lennox is a profitable US industrial manufacturer whose value is a stream of free cash flow; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2 (operating company, cyclical) with the adaptations file applied for leases, negative working-capital capture and single-charge risk. Fresh build (no prior DCF, no memory entry). FY0 = FY2025 actuals (revenue $5,195.3M, pre-SBC EBITDA $1,183.1M = 22.8%, GAAP EBITDA $1,154.0M = 22.2%); Y1 = FY2026 at guidance. Balance sheet and share count are from the 30 Jun 2026 10-Q, nine months into Y1: this means H1-2026 reported FCF (~$97M, ~$2.8/share undiscounted) is both inside the Y1 flow and already reflected in the June net debt/share count, a <1% overstatement that is more than offset by discounting the FY2026 flow a full year when only one quarter of it remains. Non-recurring items stripped from the forward path: the ~$30M Q2-2026 Section 232 tariff refund (~0.5pp of margin) is allowed to sit in the FY2026 margin only and does not carry into FY2027+; the FY2025 ~$190M A2L-transition inventory build is treated as a one-off that partly reverses in FY2026 (which is why the FY2026 FCF guide of $750-850M exceeds what the components produce), and working capital is modelled on the CHANGE in revenue at -10% capture thereafter (receivables + inventory exceed payables for a manufacturer, so growth consumes cash). D&A at 2.3% of revenue reflects H1-26 (includes NSI/Duro Dyne/Supco acquired-intangible amortisation); capex eases from 3.0% (FY2026, A2L tooling and the H1-26 run-rate of $91M) to 2.5% long-run, the FY2016-FY2025 median ex the FY2023 Saltillo plant year. Cash tax 21% flat: GAAP ETR 19.2% FY2025 and 20.6% H1-26; FY2025 cash taxes of $103.8M were a timing low against $191M expense, and are not a repeatable base. SBC held at 0.9% of revenue (mature, no decline assumed; house/street band is therefore narrow). Buyback pace: $482M FY2025, $151M H1-26, funded partly by commercial paper (CP rose $226M to $412M over the half); the model treats buybacks as value-neutral and the share count flat. The FY2026 revenue guide of +8% includes ~5 points from the NSI and Heat Controller acquisitions, so organic growth is only ~3% and the base path reflects acquisitions lapping in FY2027.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue CAGR, tempered: 5-yr 7.4% starts from the FY2020 COVID trough and the 6-yr FY2019-FY2025 CAGR is 5.3%; the base path uses FY2026 guidance (+8%, ~5pts M&A) then settles toward 5% and decays to 3% by the terminal years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR not computable: book equity was negative from FY2014 to FY2022 (cumulative buybacks exceeded retained earnings) and only turned positive in FY2023 ($393M) on the way to $1,297M at Jun-2026. EPS CAGR (18-20%) diverges far above revenue CAGR (3-7%): the gap is EBITDA margin expansion from ~15% (FY2020-22) to 22% (FY2025) plus a 24% reduction in diluted shares since FY2016, neither of which repeats at that pace. Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR of 51% is an artefact of the FY2022 trough (owner FCF $171M, working-capital build during the Refrigeration divestiture year); the 5-yr figure of 3.7% is the honest read.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC and equity-award withholding, $M): FY2016 224.6, FY2017 175.8, FY2018 347.1, FY2019 245.2, FY2020 491.7, FY2021 362.3, FY2022 171.1, FY2023 441.0, FY2024 732.0, FY2025 590.5. Owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs are within 0.1pp of each other on both windows because SBC has stayed flat at ~0.5-0.9% of revenue; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. Pre-FY2023 margins and revenue include the Refrigeration segment sold in 2022, so the pre-divestiture series is not strictly comparable.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +8% is management's reaffirmed guide (incl. ~5pts acquisitions, ~3% organic: residential volumes -12% in Q2 offset by up-to-10% Feb-2026 price increases and BCS +24%). FY2027-28 +6% as the residential replacement cycle recovers from a three-year trough (pent-up A2L-driven replacement, aging installed base) while BCS grows high-single-digit organically and acquisitions lap. Decays to 3% by FY2033, near nominal GDP, with terminal 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin is pre-SBC (SBC charged separately). FY2025 actual 22.8%; FY2026 22.0% includes the ~0.5pp Q2 tariff refund and the volume deleverage that drove the EPS guide cut. Recovery to 23.5% by FY2030 (+0.7pp over FY2025) on residential volume leverage and BCS mix; held flat thereafter, i.e. no further structural expansion beyond the already-record level.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x owner FCF for a housing-linked cyclical (method guidance 12-15x); Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x, so the cap binds. Current EV/owner-FCF on FY2025 unlevered ex-WC FCF is ~17.5x, so the terminal does not assume multiple expansion.

bull.rationale: Residential recovery arrives in 2027 as guided and is sharp (two years of deferred replacement plus A2L price/mix), BCS keeps compounding high-single to low-double digit on emergency-replacement share gains and national accounts, and the NSI/Heat Controller parts-and-supplies businesses deliver margin accretion. Pre-SBC EBITDA reaches 25% (24.1% GAAP), ~2pp above the FY2025 record, by FY2030.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands a point below the guide as H2 residential volumes deteriorate without the Q2 tariff refund; the 2027 residential recovery is pushed out again (third deferral), BCS decelerates as national-account comps and acquisition contributions lap, and competitors (Daikin/Goodman, Carrier) press price into a weak market. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin mean-reverts from the 22-23% post-COVID record toward 20% (19.1% GAAP), between the FY2023 level and today, and stays there: the market was right to re-rate the stock from 25x to 15x earnings.

scenario_narratives.base: Lennox's two axes are the timing of the US residential replacement recovery and whether post-COVID margins hold. Base: FY2026 delivers the reaffirmed +8% revenue guide (five points of it from the NSI/Duro Dyne/Supco and Heat Controller acquisitions) at an EBITDA margin a point below FY2025 after the EPS guide cut, the ~$30M Q2 tariff refund does not repeat, residential volumes stop falling in 2027 and recover gradually from a trough that is three years deep, Building Climate Solutions keeps taking emergency-replacement and national-account share at high-single-digit organic growth, and pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovers to 23.5% by FY2030 with no expansion beyond that. Working capital consumes cash as revenue grows; capex normalises to 2.5% after the A2L tooling cycle. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2027 residential rebound is sharp rather than gradual: two years of deferred replacement demand on an aging R-410A installed base meets A2L price/mix, lifting FY2027-28 revenue growth to 8-9%. BCS compounds at low-double digits on share gains and the parts/supplies acquisitions prove margin-accretive, taking pre-SBC EBITDA to 25%. Lennox's 16-year dividend record and buybacks continue to fund a flat share count. At the current price, which is near the 52-week low and ~15x earnings against a ten-year history of 20-30x, this case is where the re-rating lives.
scenario_narratives.bear: Residential affordability does not improve: the recovery slips from H2-2026 to 2027 and then again, as it already has twice, and management's credibility on timing erodes. FY2026 misses the guide as H2 lacks the tariff refund and residential deleverage worsens; commercial growth slows as acquisition contributions and national-account wins lap. Competitors press price into weak volumes and the pricing power that lifted EBITDA margins from ~15% to 22% between FY2022 and FY2025 partly reverses to ~20%. Debt-funded buybacks (commercial paper up $186M in H1-26 to $412M) slow as net debt/EBITDA approaches 1.5x. The stock's de-rating to 15x earnings turns out to be the correct mid-cycle multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because FY2026 guidance has already been cut once and the residential recovery deferred twice, and because FY2024-25 margins are a post-COVID record for a housing-linked cyclical, so mean reversion is a live path rather than a tail. Bull reduced from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right at once: a sharp 2027 residential rebound AND a further 2pp of margin on top of record levels. Base 50%: the reaffirmed revenue guide and the commercial segment's momentum make the central path credible.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a strict basis: SBC plus equity-award withholding expensed, share count held flat, working capital charged on growth, the Q2-2026 tariff refund and the FY2025 inventory build treated as one-offs, operating leases left inside EBITDA, and terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF for a housing-linked cyclical. Risk is charged once, through 25/50/25 probability weights on distinct driver paths, at a single 9% USD WACC. The valuation is anchored to the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet and the post-cut FY2026 guidance, not to the trailing peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Residential recovery timing: every year the HCS rebound slips removes roughly one year of 6% growth and the associated margin leverage; this is the dominant swing between bear and base.
Margin mean reversion: FY2024-25 EBITDA margins (21-22% GAAP) are ~6pp above the FY2016-22 range; if post-COVID pricing power fades the bear path's 20% pre-SBC level is where the business lands.

Acquisition integration and quality of growth: ~5 of the 8 points of FY2026 growth are acquired (NSI/Duro Dyne/Supco, Heat Controller); organic growth is ~3% and the parts/supplies businesses carry integration and margin risk.

Balance sheet drift: commercial paper rose from $226M to $412M in six months to fund buybacks; net debt of $1.53B is ~1.3x FY2025 EBITDA, comfortable but no longer trivial if FCF undershoots the $750-850M guide.
Terminal assumptions: ~60-70% of value sits in the terminal; the 15x cap binds in base and bull, so the valuation is more sensitive to the terminal-year margin than to any single growth year.
Data vintage: the Metrics CSV ends at Q1-2026 and its total_debt column omits commercial paper; this DCF used the Q2-2026 10-Q directly, and the CSV should be refreshed before the next update.
